Hi team,

I pulled together a first-pass rubric for the Senior Serving Engineer round and attached it (senior-serving-rubric-v2.pdf). Key changes are: tighter scope on KV cache/attention optimizations, explicit probing for compilation/kernel tradeoffs, and clearer pass/fail guidance for system design.

Request: can each of you skim and flag any +/- items by EOD tomorrow? Also: Ethan Zhou (candidate) has final onsite windows Thurs/Fri local PST — we need to lock interviewer slots.

Date: 2027-05-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rubric briefing + slot coordination for Senior Serving Eng

Thanks for the draft, Aditya — good start. A couple of quick notes after a fast read:

- Leveling: the rubric currently blends 'Senior' and 'Principal' signal in the throughput section. Suggest we add an explicit row: expected autonomy and system tradeoff ownership at Senior (OK) vs Principal (must lead architecture).
- Interview focus areas: please separate 'kernel/compilation' and 'runtime KV/cache' into two discrete probes so interviewers know which questions map to which score cell.
- Timeboxing: recommend 18m design + 18m deep-dive + 4m wrap for each panelist to keep runs comparable.

I can take point on interviewer slot coordination if you confirm which names we want on the panel. My free slots Thurs 10:00–12:00 and Fri 14:00–17:00.

Thanks — this looks good. Confirming panel and final guidance below. Please treat as the canonical plan for interviewers.

Panel (confirmed):
- Markus Klein (system design & ownership probes)
- Aditya Rao (kernel/compilation tradeoffs + perf modeling)
- Lauren Bishop (operational maturity, rollout/fallback policies)

Interviewer guidance (short):
- Use the rubric cells strictly: each cell maps to a scored question. Put numeric score in the scoring sheet (0-3).
- Red flags = immediate no-go: no ownership examples, consistently inaccurate mental model of latency sources, refusal to discuss tradeoffs.
- Gray areas: missing immediate production experience is OK if candidate shows strong vector for growth and ownership examples.

Logistics:
- Ethan's windows: Thurs 10:00–12:00 PST, Fri 14:00–17:00 PST. I blocked 10:30–12:00 Thu in my calendar for the panel. Calendar link: https://calendar.redwood.com/event/5G7H2Q
- Interview structure: 18m design -> 18m deep dive -> 4m wrap and scoring. Please keep notes in the shared Drive folder.

Attachments: [Attachment: scoring-cheatsheet.csv (CSV)], [Attachment: candidate-brief-ethan-zhou.pdf (PDF)]
